meta.title: Texas's 23rd Congressional District: No Special Election

district.vacancy_reason: The seat became vacant after Rep. Tony Gonzales resigned. No special election was called: the seat stays vacant until the winner of the regular general of November 3, 2026 is sworn in.

district_context.note: The party-level projection below is the last provisional one, frozen when the desk closed. The seat is decided on November 3 under the 2026 map, in the House projection.

assumptions.label: 119th Congress district
assumptions.note: The anchor uses the district that elected the departing member, not a later general-election redistricting plan.

assumptions.label: Candidate field pending
assumptions.note: Candidate-specific effects are not applied before official qualification.

assumptions.label: Special-election uncertainty
assumptions.note: The distribution is deliberately wider than a normal general-election projection because date, turnout and nominees remain unknown.

assumptions.label: No special election
assumptions.note: No writ was ever issued. Six months after the vacancy and days before the regular general, the seat is left vacant until November 3; this desk is closed and its projection kept unchanged as a record.

no_writ_fallback.note: No writ was issued, so the seat is not filled by a special election at all: it stays vacant until the regular general of November 3, 2026, whose winner is sworn in January 2027. That contest runs on the 2026 map and is covered by the House projection, not by this desk.

method_note: Closed desk. The figures are the last provisional party-control projection, made while a special election was still expected: it anchors to the 119th Congress district result and widens uncertainty for special-election turnout and candidate effects. No special election was called — see pending.no_writ_fallback for the contest that fills the seat.
